blurb: Overhead lines, underground and subsea cable, HVDC, transformers and switchgear, protection and control, stability services, and the distribution edge — with voltage class, lead time, and how hard each one is to site.
question: How do you move this power, and what is actually in the way?
title: Grid and Transmission: A Practical Reference
lede: Generation gets the headlines; the grid decides what actually gets built. This guide catalogs {{N_ENTRIES}} technologies across seven classes, from 765 kV overhead line to the smart meter on a house, with the voltage class each one serves, what it costs in time rather than dollars, and how much of the schedule is engineering against how much is right-of-way.

facets.label: Voltage
facets.tip: Voltage class the technology normally serves. LV under 1 kV · MV 1–35 kV, the distribution feeders · HV 35–230 kV, subtransmission and smaller transmission · EHV 230–800 kV, the bulk system · UHV above 800 kV, built at scale only in China and India. Most equipment spans a band.

facets.label: Role
facets.tip: What the technology is bought to do. Most equipment does more than one job, and the reason a utility buys it is often the second one on the list.

facets.label: Lead time
facets.tip: Time from decision to energization for a typical project, including procurement but not litigation. This is the number that has changed most since 2021: large power transformers and HVDC converters both went from months to years, and on many projects the equipment now arrives after the permits.

facets.label: Siting
facets.tip: How hard the technology is to permit and place. Inside the fence = goes in an existing substation or on existing structures · Corridor = needs an existing right of way · New right of way = needs land nobody has agreed to yet, which is where most large projects die.

facets.label: Maturity
facets.tip: Mature = installed for decades, many vendors · Established = commercial with a shorter record or fewer suppliers · Emerging = deployed but still proving itself at scale · Early = pilots and demonstrations.
